sources.section: Document Management - Institutional Repository and Digital Library Software
sources.entry: DSpace - Turnkey repository application providing durable access to digital resources. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Java

summary.one_liner: DSpace is an open source, Java-based turnkey repository application for providing durable access to digital resources, used by institutions and libraries.
summary.what_it_does: DSpace is the backend of a repository system, a Java web application that exposes a REST API plus other machine-facing interfaces such as OAI-PMH and SWORD. It is paired with an Angular-based frontend that serves as the user interface built on that REST API. The README states it requires a PostgreSQL database and a servlet container, usually Tomcat. The README describes the project's documentation, release, wiki, and mailing list resources, and it points to developer guidelines for code style and conventions. It also documents how to run unit and integration tests with Maven, including single-test and single-module runs. The README gives no details on specific repository features such as ingest workflows, metadata schemas, or search.
use_cases: Running an institutional repository for a university or library
Providing durable long-term access to digital resources
Exposing repository content via OAI-PMH harvesting
Depositing items through SWORD-based submission tools
Hosting a digital library with a REST API backend
how_to_run: Install prerequisites: PostgreSQL database and a servlet container such as Tomcat (see the installation docs linked in the README)
Build the backend with Maven: mvn install
Run only unit tests: mvn test -DskipUnitTests=false
Run only integration tests: mvn install -DskipIntegrationTests=false
Quick-start development or testing setup: Docker Compose scripts (see 'Running DSpace with Docker Compose' in the README)
notable: Turnkey institutional repository used by more than 2,000 organizations according to the README
Split architecture: Java backend REST API with a separate Angular frontend
Supports machine interfaces such as OAI-PMH and SWORD
Quick-start Docker Compose scripts for development and testing
caveats: The README says there are no production-ready Docker images; Docker Compose scripts are for development or testing only
Requires a separate PostgreSQL database and servlet container, so setup is nontrivial
Unit and integration tests are disabled by default and must be enabled with Maven flags
